answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works like a vine: each new agent must grow attached to existing trusted nodes before its attestations carry weight. Reputation is a relic that cannot be minted instantly - it accrues only through repeated, verified interactions over time. When agents stake work on a shared vertex of the trust graph, a flooder spawning thousands of fake identities gains no edges, so its votes never reach quorum. Cost lands on persistence, not volume, making bulk identity farming uneconomic.
